items.title: Existence, uniqueness and finiteness of the scheme theoretic support of a finite type quasi-coherent module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the scheme theoretic support of a finite type quasi-coherent module as the smallest closed subscheme from which the module can be pushed forward, and states its affine description by annihilators together with uniqueness, finiteness and the identification of supports (statement lines 945-961). The counted proof uses the closed subscheme/module equivalence to obtain uniqueness and minimality, the affine dictionary to get finiteness and supports, and then reduces the existence of the closed subscheme to the quasi-coherence of the annihilator ideal, which is the compatibility of annihilators of finite modules with localization (proof lines 963-986). It is H2: the organisation of the argument is carried out in the counted span; the only thing the author leaves to the reader is the elementary localization statement, which is named explicitly in the span.
